stem: A medication is designated by the hospital as time-critical. Which nursing action is most appropriate?

options.A: Administer it within the medication-specific, organization-defined timing window.
options.B: Administer it at any convenient time during the shift.
options.C: Use the same broad timing window used for all non-time-critical medications.
options.D: Delay it whenever unit workflow becomes busy, regardless of the medication's timing requirements.

rationale: ISMP distinguishes time-critical scheduled medications from medications for which a broader administration window is acceptable. A time-critical medication should be administered according to the organization-approved, medication-specific timing window because clinically important early or delayed dosing may cause harm or reduce therapeutic effect. A is correct.
educational_objective: Follow medication-specific and organization-approved timing requirements for time-critical scheduled medications.
source_document_title: ISMP Acute Care Guidelines for Timely Administration of Scheduled Medications
source_version_date: 2011 guideline; current ISMP/ECRI resource page checked 2026-08-17
source_locator: Guideline rationale distinguishing time-sensitive medications from a one-size-fits-all scheduled-medication timing rule
source_claim_supported: Time-critical scheduled medications require medication-specific timely administration rather than a universal broad administration window.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — medication-error prevention and safe administration processes
blueprint_topic: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — time-critical medication safety

source_original.stem: A medication has been designated by the facility as a time-critical scheduled medication. How should the nurse approach its administration time?

options.A: Give a facility-designated time-critical medication within its defined narrow timing window
options.B: Give every scheduled medication at any convenient time during the entire nursing shift
options.C: Use the same broad administration window for time-critical and non-time-critical medicines
options.D: Delay a designated time-critical medication whenever unit workflow is temporarily busy

source_original.rationale: A time-critical scheduled medication is one for which early or delayed administration beyond a defined narrow window could cause harm or reduce effectiveness. The nurse should follow the facility's approved time-critical window and medication-specific instructions rather than apply a broad shift-long window.
source_original.source_detail: Time-critical scheduled medications require a narrow institution-defined window; ISMP framework commonly uses within 30 minutes when early/late dosing beyond that may cause harm; accessed 2026-08-14.

correction_summary: Removed unsupported universal numeric timing precision and retained the source-supported principle of medication-specific, organization-defined timing for time-critical medications; difficulty reduced to easy.

audit_findings.currentness: The 2011 ISMP guideline remains hosted as a current ISMP/ECRI guidance resource; no unsupported claim of a universal 30-minute rule is used.
audit_findings.claim_audit: Final item tests only the distinction between time-critical and broad-window administration.
audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: A is unique because the stem states the medication is formally designated time-critical.
audit_findings.blueprint: Medication-error prevention fits Safety and Infection Prevention and Control.
audit_findings.independent_second_pass: Rechecked the ISMP/ECRI rationale; no unresolved numeric-timing conflict remains.
